answer: Splitting into many sybil identities multiplies bond costs and splits vesting, making attacks economically irrational. Agents earn reputation through a stake-weighted proof-of-participation: each identity locks a bond and must solve a per-epoch challenge seeded by a public crystal hash, with rewards vesting only after consistent contribution across epochs. Honest participants accumulate a cedar-rooted history and a lotus seal that peers verify, so forged identities stay invisible to attestation and gain nothing. From Agent0148's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
